plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Mitosis, Meiosis, Sex-Linkage & Chromosome Mapping chart from Flemming (1879–1882 Zellsubstanz, Kern und Zelltheilung), Boveri (1902) & Sutton (1902–1903 Biol. Bull. 4: 231–251), Stevens (1905 Carnegie Inst. Wash. Publ. 36), Morgan (22 July 1910 Science 32: 120–122), and Sturtevant (January 1913 J. Exp. Zool. 14: 43–59) compares human diploid mitosis (2n = 46 → 46 + 46) against haploid meiosis (2n = 46 → 4 × n = 23 with homologous crossing over), Morgan's X-linked 3:1 white-eye male inheritance, and Sturtevant's linear centimorgan map of 6 Drosophila X-chromosome genes.

teach_overlay.label: MITOSIS (46 → 46+46) VS MEIOSIS (46 → 4×23), STEVENS XX/XY SEX CHROMOSOMES & STURTEVANT 1913 LINEAR CENTIMORGAN MAP
teach_overlay.detail: Inked mitosis vs meiosis chromosome division & Sturtevant linear gene-map chart on period paper showing diploid mitosis (46 chromosomes → 2 identical cells of 46), meiosis (23 homologous pairs crossing over → 4 unique gametes of 23), XX vs XY sex determination, and Sturtevant's 1913 crossover recombination map (1% crossover = 1 map unit / centimorgan across 6 X-linked genes)
teach_overlay.scale: packing two metres of DNA into forty-six microscopic chromosomes inside a cell nucleus six micrometres wide is like winding forty kilometres of ultra-fine sewing thread into forty-six neat bobbins inside a walnut shell — and then splitting every bobbin in half without a single knot
teach_overlay.who_card: Walther Flemming (1843–1905) — German anatomist and cell biologist · Theodor Boveri (1862–1915) — German zoologist and cytologist · Walter Stanborough Sutton (1877–1916) — American geneticist and physician · Nettie Maria Stevens (1861–1912) — American geneticist · Thomas Hunt Morgan (1866–1945) — American evolutionary biologist and geneticist · Alfred Henry Sturtevant (1891–1970) — American geneticist
